They were really good. I can't fault this game on anything that comes to mind. This game is definitely beatable but it requires patience. Made by Aussie devs which is awesome! I recommend Hollow Knight. It's not always hard and there are plenty of benches/hot springs around. And you get a second chance to regain your geo. Take your time and enjoy it.

There's not much that's memorable about the journey beyond the first couple of hours. After that, it becomes a slog of fighting the same enemies in different parts of the map. Some boss fights were neat, but most were more annoying than challenging. You finally get a new weapon after trekking across half the map, try it out, and you're left with an "oh, that's it?" feeling. 

I don't regret playing it, but I can't say I'd recommend it enthusiastically.

I am coming back to this game after 4-5 years and (DESPITE IT'S ANNOYING WAY OF HANDLING DIFFICULTY), it has some of the smoothest platforming I have ever played. The visuals are absolutely phenomenal, and the soundtrack is practically transcendent. Although its runtime is incredibly short, it is worth each and every second of your time. The abilities feel smooth and responsive, each one goes together near perfectly, and even when you only have a third of them, you still feel like you're one with the character once you get the hang of the movement.

TL:DR: Phenomenal game all around, but do be aware that the later areas end up feeling more tedious and annoying than actually difficult (I'm looking at you, Sorrow Pass).

Its an indie masterpiece. Music and story are awesome and the gameplay is very short and satisfying. Took me 8 hours to complete the game yet it feels like 80.

Its worth your money and if you are a fan of solemn and somber settings this game is definitely for you.
Combat and spell variety is consistent and I have found every spell and weapon to be reasonably powerful.
It runs well on all platforms and has pixel art style which gives enormous performance boost.
Highly recommend 9/10!
